name: Starting a new product with no code yet

failureModes.prompt: Should the accounts for hosting, the domain and the app stores belong to the business instead of one person's login?
failureModes.why: when the only login belongs to someone who leaves, the business can lose access to its own app, domain or data

options.label: Accounts owned by the business
options.consequence: a shared company email and a second admin to set up, and access continues when people leave

options.label: One person's login for now
options.consequence: quickest today, and moving apps, domains and billing to the business later takes time and support requests

failureModes.provenBy: a written list of every outside account showing a business email as owner and at least two people with admin access

failureModes.prompt: Should passwords and keys for outside services be kept out of the code from the first day?
failureModes.why: a key saved in the code once stays in its history after deletion, and anyone who sees the history can use it

options.label: Keep them out from the first commit
options.consequence: a few minutes of setup now, and the code can be shared without replacing keys

options.label: Put them in the code for now
options.consequence: faster today, and every key must be replaced before anyone else sees the code

failureModes.recommended: Keep them out from the first commit
failureModes.provenBy: a secret scan of the whole history, for example with gitleaks, that finds no keys and runs on every push

failureModes.prompt: Will each saved item belong to one person, or to an account that several people can share?
failureModes.why: whose data each record is decides every later query, screen and permission, and changing it after launch means reworking each of them

options.label: An account that can hold several people
options.consequence: one more column in each table now, and both single users and teams fit later

options.label: The person who created it
options.consequence: simplest now, and adding shared team spaces later means reworking every table and query

failureModes.recommended: An account that can hold several people
failureModes.provenBy: a schema check that every table holding customer data has a required owner column, and a test that one account cannot read another account's rows

failureModes.prompt: Should there be a separate test copy of the product, with its own data, before real people use it?
failureModes.why: without one, every test and every half-finished change runs against real customers and their data

options.label: Separate test and live copies
options.consequence: two of everything to run and pay for, and tests never use real people's data

options.label: One copy for everything
options.consequence: cheaper and simpler, and every test or mistake reaches real customers

failureModes.provenBy: a check that the test copy uses a different database and different keys from the live copy, and that a test sign-up never appears in live data

failureModes.prompt: Where should the product run once it is public: a managed platform or servers we rent and maintain?
failureModes.why: the hosting choice limits which tools and languages the product can use, so choosing it after building can force a rewrite

options.label: A managed platform
options.consequence: less to maintain, and some kinds of long-running work need a separate service

options.label: Servers we rent and maintain
options.consequence: full control, and someone must install security updates and monitor them

failureModes.provenBy: a recorded hosting choice in the repository, and a first deployment of an empty page to that host before features are built

failureModes.prompt: If the stored data were lost today, how many hours of recent work would be acceptable to lose?
failureModes.why: it sets how often backups run and what they cost, and a backup nobody has restored may not work when needed

options.label: A few minutes, with continuous backups
options.consequence: costs more each month, and almost nothing is lost

options.label: Up to a day, with nightly backups
options.consequence: cheaper, and up to a day of everyone's work can disappear

failureModes.recommended: A few minutes, with continuous backups
failureModes.provenBy: a restore of the latest backup into a scratch database, timed and checked against the chosen window before launch
